Order intake notes:

- Form v1 requires: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Source records may use alternate names: customer -> cust; quantity -> qty. Always normalize these before validation.
- Do not assume a field is valid merely because it is present; validate all required fields and value formats, especially priority, qty, and ship_country.
- Preserve valid values across retries and correct only fields identified as invalid. Repeated retries can still fail if invalid fields are copied unchanged.
- A successful submission contained normalized cust/email/order_date plus valid priority, qty, and ship_country. ORD-5101 and ORD-5109 were accepted.
- Front-desk statements such as “duplicate check already done,” confirmation calls, or portal origin are context only, not validation evidence.
- Treat attempts for the same customer/order as retries when indicated; after attempt 3 fails, route to manual review.

Order intake notes:

- Form versions 1–3 require: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Validate the applicable form’s required fields and formats; versions observed so far use the same field set.
- Normalize alternate source names before validation: customer → cust; quantity → qty. Do not treat truncated, missing, or malformed values as valid.
- Validate every required field, especially priority, qty, and ship_country. Presence alone is insufficient.
- On retries, preserve values that already passed validation and correct only fields identified as invalid. Recheck all fields after each correction; unchanged invalid values can cause repeated rejection.
- Attempts with the same customer/order details may appear under successive batch IDs. Track them as one retry sequence when indicated, regardless of front-desk submitter or form version.
- Front-desk claims (“duplicate check done,” portal origin, confirmation call, handwritten transcription, or stated priority) are context only, not validation evidence.
- After attempt 3 fails, stop automated retries and route the record to manual review.
- Successful examples: ORD-5101, ORD-5109, ORD-5114, and ORD-5119. ORD-5114 succeeded on attempt 2 after correction; ORD-5119 succeeded on attempt 2 after correcting invalid priority/ship_country while retaining valid data.

Order intake notes:

- Form versions 1–4 observed so far require: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Validate the applicable form’s required fields, formats, and values; presence alone is insufficient.
- Normalize alternate source names before validation: customer → cust; quantity → qty. Do not accept truncated, missing, malformed, or invalid values.
- Validate every required field, especially priority, qty, and ship_country. If extra status-related data is supplied, validate it as well; an invalid status can cause rejection.
- On retries, preserve values that passed validation and correct only fields identified as invalid. Recheck every field after each correction; a previously invalid or unchanged field can cause another rejection.
- Group successive batches into one retry sequence only when customer and order details match. A shared customer is not enough: changed email or order_date indicates a distinct sequence.
- Front-desk claims (duplicate check, portal origin, confirmation request, transcription, or stated priority) are context only, not validation evidence.
- After attempt 3 fails, stop automated retries and route the record to manual review.
- Recent outcomes: Eli Reyes succeeded on attempt 2 after priority/ship_country correction (ORD-5120/5121). Ada Sato exhausted all 3 attempts and went to manual review (ORD-5122–5124). Dee Reyes sequence ORD-5125–5127 exhausted attempts; ORD-5128/5129 is a separate sequence and remained invalid at attempt 2.
- Prior successful examples: ORD-5101, ORD-5109, ORD-5114, and ORD-5119; ORD-5114 and ORD-5119 succeeded on attempt 2 after targeted corrections.

Order intake notes:

- Normalize source names before validation: customer → cust; quantity → qty. Reject truncated, missing, malformed, or invalid values.
- Use ISO date format YYYY-MM-DD. Slash-form dates such as 03/22/2026 or 02/18/2026 are invalid, even when the date is otherwise correct.
- Validate every required field, especially priority, qty, and ship_country. Validate any supplied status-related data too; invalid status can cause rejection.
- Front-desk claims (duplicate checks, portal origin, confirmations, transcription, or stated priority) are context only, not validation evidence.
- On retries, preserve values that passed validation and correct only identified invalid fields. Recheck every field after each correction; unchanged or newly invalid fields can cause rejection.
- Group successive batches into one retry sequence only when customer and order details match. Shared customer alone is insufficient; changed email or order_date means a distinct sequence.
- After attempt 3 fails, stop automated retries and route the record to manual review.

Eli Okafor ORD-5134–5136 exhausted all attempts and went to manual review. Cy Okafor ORD-5137–5139 exhausted all attempts; the final rejection also included invalid status.
- Prior successful examples: ORD-5101, ORD-5109, ORD-5114, and ORD-5119; ORD-5114 and ORD-5119 succeeded on attempt 2 after targeted corrections.

Order intake notes:

- Normalize source names before validation: customer → cust, email → contact_email, quantity → qty. Use the form’s canonical field names and avoid retaining conflicting aliases (such as both email and contact_email).
- Reject truncated, missing, malformed, or invalid values. Dates must be ISO YYYY-MM-DD; partial dates such as 2026-03 or 2026-12- are invalid.
